bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: A long-legged doji candle features identical or near-identical open and close prices paired with exceptionally long upper and lower wicks, representing extreme market volatility and indecision where price swings wildly in both directions.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A doji candle is characterized by an opening and closing price that are identical or very close together... The long legged doji features exceptionally long upper and lower wicks relative to its body. It represents extreme market volatility and indecision.

facts.statement: Anna Coulling refers to the long-legged doji as a 'daddy long legs' because its elongated upper and lower wicks resemble the small flying insect with very long legs.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Should resemble what I used to call, a 'daddy long legs' – a small flying insect with very long legs!

facts.statement: Unlike hammers or shooting stars, a long-legged doji must be validated by average, high, or ultra-high volume to confirm genuine market indecision and high effort behind the wide price swings.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A long legged doji candle, should always be validated by a minimum of average volume, and preferably high or ultra high. If it is low, then it is an anomaly.

facts.statement: Low volume on a long-legged doji is a major anomaly because wide price swings (large result) on low volume (lack of effort) violate Wyckoff's Third Law, signaling stop-hunting and insider price-racking.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Unlike shooting stars or hammers, low volume on a long legged doji is a major anomaly... The market has moved sharply in both directions and finally closed back near the opening price... no effort (low volume) and a big result.

facts.statement: High-impact fundamental news releases like the monthly U.S. Non-Farm Payroll (NFP) data trigger rapid volume surges and intense price volatility, creating repeated long-legged doji candles as the market whipsaws violently.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: High-impact fundamental news releases... trigger rapid volume surges and intense price volatility... The long legged doji is seen most often during a fundamental news release, and the classic one for the US markets is the monthly Non Farm Payroll data.

facts.statement: When economic news is released, volume validates the move: a price surge on high/rising volume confirms insider participation, while a price move on low volume indicates a trap move and insider inaction.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Whenever we have an economic release... the associated volume reaction will instantly tell us whether the market is validating the news or ignoring it... If the volume surge has validated the price move, then we can be sure that the insiders are joining in.

facts.statement: Market makers use quiet periods or news catalysts to push prices across key levels on low volume, 'racking' the price to trigger retail stop-loss and limit orders without committing capital for their own accounts.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The most common reason for this is stop hunting, where the market makers and insiders are moving prices violently, first one way and then the other, to shake traders out, and to take out stop and limit orders in the process.

facts.statement: Stopping volume occurs when high volume enters a sharply falling market (bearish price waterfall) where professional money steps in over two to three sessions to buy and halt further price decline.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: High volume entering a sharply falling market (bearish price waterfall) where professional money moves in to buy and halt further price decline. It is the precursor to an accumulation phase and buying climax.

facts.statement: Topping-out volume arcs form when an uptrend runs out of steam as insiders distribute inventory into retail FOMO, causing price spreads to narrow, upper wicks to lengthen, and successive peaks to form a curved arcing pattern on high volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A visual price-and-volume pattern indicating that an uptrend is running out of steam and topping out as professional traders distribute inventory into retail FOMO... successive candles form a distinct curved 'arcing pattern'.

facts.topic: Wide vs. Narrow Spread Volume Rules
facts.statement: Wide-spread candles require high volume to be validated and low volume indicates a trap, whereas narrow-spread candles validate low volume while high volume indicates insider absorption or resistance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wide Spread Candle: Above-average / High Volume validates... Low Volume is Anomaly... Narrow Spread Candle: Low Volume validates... High / Ultra-High Volume indicates insider resistance or absorption.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
